summary: Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (University of Kelaniya) and as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Asen Balikci was a historian, archaeologist, and anthropologist who completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1956. He held posts at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel, the Canadian Museum of History, and the University of Montreal (1963–1993).

Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD in philosophy at Brandeis University (~1965–1969). He was the Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College (~1968–2020) and founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and served as professor and head of philosophy at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and Banaras Hindu University.
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1966). He founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

Ashok Narhar Aklujkar is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held positions at Pune University, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1967–1989).

Ashutosh Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian who studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served on the Calcutta High Court, presided over the Asiatic Society and the University of Calcutta, and founded Asutosh College in 1916.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta (~1962–1967) under D. Mukherjee. He served as a senior research fellow at the University of Calcutta and lectured at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, the Academy of Finland, and the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist and historian who studied at St. John's College, Johannesburg, Selwyn College, and SOAS University of London. He joined the faculty of the University of Cape Town in 1923.
Athanaric Huard is an Indologist who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. He is an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Atsuhiko Yoshida is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Seikei, Tokyo, Strasbourg, EPHE, and Athénée Français under Georges Dumézil. He held posts at CNRS, Geneva, UCLA, Seikei University, and Gakushuin University.

Atsuki Nakagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakagami held a visiting researcher post at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and an affiliation with the Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989). He serves as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Meteorological College (~1985–1993) and Komazawa University (~1993–2003).
Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indologist who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under T. R. V. Murti and others. He held academic posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima, and Kindai universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Doshisha and Kyoto universities under Ryosaburo Sakaki, later serving as professor at Kyoto University and Tokai University, and president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies.
